story_type: teen sailors in a swamped dinghy in high wind, Coast Guard surface swimmer jumps in and brings them to the lifeboat
hook: Seven sailboats in trouble at once. Two teens still on this one.
narration: Two teenage sailors were stuck on a small boat that was filling with water.
Strong winds had overwhelmed a group of sailors on Tomales Bay, California.
Their yacht club called the Coast Guard. Seven of its sailboats, two sailors on each, were in trouble.
Three had capsized. The rest were swamped by the weather.
A forty-seven foot lifeboat crew came out from Station Bodega Bay.
Petty Officer Daniel Langley went over the side as the surface swimmer.
He swam out to the sailboat through the chop.
The water was in the low fifties. A wetsuit traps a thin layer of water that the body warms, which holds off hypothermia.
[short pause] One at a time, he brought both teens back to the lifeboat.
outcome: Both teens were pulled aboard, and the yacht club's safety boat brought the other twelve sailors ashore.
title: Swimmer jumps in for 2 teen sailors
description:
On July 2, 2019, a Coast Guard Station Bodega Bay surface swimmer brought two teenage sailors from their swamped sailboat aboard a 47-foot motor lifeboat on Tomales Bay, California, after strong winds overwhelmed seven yacht club sailboats.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Jordan Akiyama, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/694919/coast-guard-station-bodega-bay-rescues-two-tomales-bay
